title: The second boon: the fire that leads to heaven
theme: Naciketas asks Death, who knows it, to teach him the fire whose builders reach immortality in heaven.

words.context: Śaṅkara: «स्वर्गो लोको येषां ते स्वर्गलोकाः यजमानाः»
Śaṅkara: «अमृतत्वम् अमरणतां देवत्वं» — the immortality of the gods

sandhi.rule: Final m before a vowel stays m and joins the next word.
The visarga of -āḥ is lost before a vowel and the hiatus stays: P. 8.3.17 (भोभगोअघोअपूर्वस्य योऽशि), P. 8.3.22 (हलि सर्वेषाम्) for consonants.

sandhi.type: e before a vowel; t before d
sandhi.rule: e before a vowel becomes ay and the y is dropped, P. 6.1.78 (एचोऽयवायावः) and P. 8.3.19 (लोपः शाकल्यस्य); final t before d becomes d, P. 8.2.39 (झलां जशोऽन्ते).

samasa.meaning: those whose world is heaven (the sacrificers who reach it)

morphology.note: Present of adhi-i ‘go over, learn, know’; Śaṅkara glosses ‘you remember, you know’.
svarga + the suffix ya ‘for the sake of’: ‘conducive to heaven’. Raṅgarāmānuja cites the rule: «‘स्वर्गादिभ्यो यद्वक्तव्यः’ इति प्रयोजनम् इत्यर्थे यत्».
Present middle participle of śrad-dhā ‘put faith’, dative: ‘to [me who am] faithful’.

translation.literal: ‘You, O Death, know the fire that leads to heaven; declare it to me who have faith. Those whose world is heaven enjoy immortality. This I choose with the second boon.’
translation.readable: ‘You know the fire that leads to heaven, Death. Teach it to me, for I have faith. Those who reach heaven gain immortality — this is my second wish.’

syntax: sa tvam … adhyeṣi ‘you, that one, know’ is followed by the request prabrūhi tam ‘declare it’. A general statement about the heaven-dwellers (svargalokā amṛtatvaṃ bhajante) gives the reason, and etad dvitīyena vṛṇe vareṇa closes the request formally.

ambiguities.note: Śaṅkara: the immortality of the gods, a long but not absolute deathlessness: «अमृतत्वम् अमरणतां देवत्वं भजन्ते». Raṅgarāmānuja: those whose world is heaven are those who have reached the highest abode, «परमपदं प्राप्ता इत्यर्थः».
The vishvAsa mūla reads tvaṃ, ‘you’, for taṃ, ‘it’ (the fire); Śaṅkara comments on taṃ (corrections.json).

beginner: Having described heaven, Naciketas makes his second request. You, Death, he says, know the fire ritual that takes people to heaven. Teach it to me, because I have faith. People who reach heaven by it gain immortality. That is my second wish. The fire here is a real Vedic ritual: an altar built of bricks on which the sacred fire is laid. Naciketas asks for the knowledge of it, not only its performance. Note his faith: he presents himself as a student ready to learn, and that readiness is what the Upaniṣad values.
analogy: Like a student who, before asking the deepest question, first asks the teacher to show the craft that the teacher is known for.

commentary.label: direct
commentary.text: The knowledge of the fire that leads to heaven, from Death, who knows it, for a student who has faith. Its fruit: those who reach heaven by it enjoy immortality.

commentary.q: What does Śaṅkara say the fire is?
commentary.label: traditional
commentary.text: The means of reaching the heaven just described: «एवं गुणविशिष्टस्य स्वर्गलोकस्य प्राप्तिसाधनभूतम् अग्निं». The immortality is the gods’ deathlessness, not the self-knowledge of the third boon: «अमृतत्वम् अमरणतां देवत्वं भजन्ते».

commentary.label: comparative
commentary.text: Raṅgarāmānuja takes heaven as release (see 1.1.12) and the fire as serving it through meditation: «स्थण्डिलरूपाग्ने: स्वर्गप्रयोजनकत्वञ्चउपासनाद्वारेति उत्तरत्र स्फुटम्». The faithful one is faithful to release: «मोक्षश्रद्धावते».

commentary.label: traditional
commentary.text: Madhva’s half-verse on 1.1.12–13: the fire is Hari, present in the Nāciketa fire and called Agni for being foremost (agrya): «अग्र्यत्वादग्निनामासौ नाचिकेताग्निगो हरिः».

advaita.text: A request for a ritual knowledge whose fruit is heaven and relative immortality, «अमरणतां देवत्वं». It belongs to the realm of action; the third boon will ask for what lies beyond action.

visistadvaita.text: The fire serves release by way of meditation, and those ‘whose world is heaven’ have reached the highest abode: «परमपदं प्राप्ता इत्यर्थः».

dvaita.text: The ‘fire’ asked for is Hari, who is in the Nāciketa fire: «नाचिकेताग्निगो हरिः». What is sought through the ritual is the Lord.

schools.disagreement: All three take the fire as a real ritual; they differ on its fruit. Śaṅkara: heaven and the gods’ immortality. Raṅgarāmānuja: release, through meditation. Madhva: Hari as the true object behind the fire.

contemporary.text: Naciketas asks the master for his craft and offers his trust in return. Good learning still begins that way: with a request to someone who knows, and a willingness to take the teaching seriously before judging it. (A modern reflection.)

reflect.beginner: Whom would you ask to teach you something they are known for?
reflect.deeper: Is there a difference between living forever and being free of death?
reflect.practice: Before your next question to a teacher or colleague, say plainly why you want to know.

flags.note: The vishvAsa mūla reads tvaṃ for taṃ (‘you’ for ‘it’); Madhva’s text writes bhajante etad without the sandhi. Both listed in corrections.json.
